title: Chapter 12 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of accessibility leadership, culture, legal landscape, and action planning.

questions.question: What is the primary reason to frame accessibility as a business case?
options: To align accessibility with strategic goals like revenue, risk, and brand, gaining leadership buy‑in
It's the only way to get budget
questions.explanation: A business case translates accessibility into value that leaders care about.

questions.question: Which US law is often cited in website accessibility lawsuits?
questions.explanation: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is the primary law for web accessibility lawsuits in the US.

questions.question: A VPAT is a mandatory government certification that proves your product is fully accessible.
questions.explanation: A VPAT is a self‑declaration template, not a certification. It documents the state of accessibility but does not guarantee compliance.

questions.question: What is the European Accessibility Act (EAA) expected to enforce?
options: WCAG 2.1 AA for many private sector products and services
questions.explanation: The EAA will apply broadly, requiring WCAG conformance for products and services sold in the EU.

questions.question: A _____ is a document that details how a product conforms to accessibility standards, often used in procurement.
questions.explanation: VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) is the industry standard.

questions.question: In a proactive accessibility culture, who is responsible for accessibility?
questions.explanation: A mature culture embeds accessibility into every role.

questions.question: An accessibility champion network is a one‑time effort to fix all issues.
questions.explanation: A champion network is an ongoing governance and advocacy structure to sustain accessibility.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of an accessibility maturity model?
options: To punish teams that aren't accessible
To assess current capabilities and plan improvements
To generate a score for marketing
questions.explanation: Maturity models provide a framework for continuous improvement.

questions.question: An organization that integrates accessibility into design systems, CI, and training is likely at which maturity stage?
questions.explanation: Proactive organizations have embedded accessibility into their standard processes.

questions.question: What is a good early KPI to track in an accessibility program?
options: Automated accessibility violations count over time
questions.explanation: Reducing automated violations is a tangible, measurable early indicator.

questions.question: Why is involving people with disabilities in usability testing crucial?
options: It satisfies a specific WCAG criterion
They can identify real‑world barriers that automated tools and checklists miss
questions.explanation: Users with lived experience reveal practical barriers and contextual issues.

questions.question: You should force usability test participants to use only the screen reader you provide so results are consistent.
questions.explanation: Participants should use their own familiar assistive technology to reflect real‑world usage.

questions.question: What is co‑design?
options: Designing alongside users with disabilities as equal partners
questions.explanation: Co‑design involves users directly in the creative process.

questions.question: Which professional certification focuses on web accessibility?
questions.explanation: IAAP's WAS certification validates technical web accessibility expertise.

questions.question: What does 'shift left' mean in the context of accessibility?
options: Testing earlier in the development lifecycle
Moving all a11y work to the design team
questions.explanation: Shift left integrates testing and quality earlier, reducing cost and rework.

questions.question: Once a website passes an accessibility audit, no further work is needed.
questions.explanation: Accessibility requires continuous monitoring and improvement as content and code change.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to maintain accessibility momentum in an organization?
options: Regular audits, ongoing training, and visible leadership support
Fixing issues only when users complain
questions.explanation: Sustained effort across people, process, and technology is essential.

questions.question: Why is inclusive hiring important for an accessibility program?
options: Employees with disabilities provide invaluable firsthand perspective on barriers
questions.explanation: Diverse teams build more inclusive products.

questions.question: What is the key message when presenting an accessibility business case to executives?
options: It's the law, so we have to
Accessibility drives revenue, reduces risk, and strengthens our brand
It's a nice thing to do
questions.explanation: Executives respond to strategic value: risk, revenue, and reputation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of an organization at the 'Innovative' accessibility maturity stage?
options: Accessibility is a competitive advantage and drives product innovation
questions.explanation: Innovative organizations go beyond compliance to lead the market.
